newsitem.title: USA: Ryder earnings jump, sets early retirement plan.
newsitem.headline: Ryder earnings jump, sets early retirement plan.

text.p: Ryder System Inc. Monday reported a 26 percent rise in third quarter profits, but it announced a cost reduction plan that could affect 1,000 workers through early retirement.

The truck leasing and automotive carrier firm said its net earnings rose to $26.3 million, or 32 cents a share, in the third quarter from $20.9 million, or 26 cents a share, a year ago. Last year's results were impacted by a strike against Ryder Automotive Carrier Services, which transports autos to car dealers, by the International Brotherhood of Teamsters.
Revenues increased to $1.41 billion from $1.26 billion.

Ryder said it planned to take a restructuring charge of between $75 million and $150 million in the fourth quarter related to a voluntary retirement programme involving some 1,000 U.S. hourly and salaried employees of Ryder System and Ryder Transportation Services.

"We expect to make the announcement before the end of the year of a charge, and ... it should be in the neighbourhood of $75 to $150 million," Ryder System Chairman Anthony Burns said in a conference call.
He said areas that the company was looking at included its market coverage, headquarters staff, vehicle and non-vehicle purchasing and facilities utilization.
"Most of the improvement should become more evident in the first quarter of 1997," he said.
The company has a total workforce of 44,000 people.
Ryder said retirement dates for employees who elect to participate will be Jan. 1, Feb. 1 or March 1, 1997. About 1,000 employees are eligible for the programme.

Employees who elect to take the voluntary retirement programme would receive a pension benefit enhanced by an additional three years added to the employee's age and three years added to the employee's service with the company.
Ryder said the cost of the fourth-quarter restructuring would offset the gain from the sale of its Consumer Truck Rental business unit, which was completed on Oct. 17, for $575 million in cash.
"Cash has been received and we're starting to pay down debt," Ryder Chief Financial Officer Edwin Huston said.
The company also announced that it will buy back up to six million of its shares.
Burns said the share buyback programme would be on the open market and would begin soon.
"We would anticipate that we would conclude it within three to four months," he said.
Ryder's stock was up $1.375 to $30 on the New York Stock Exchange.
